summary: JOIN combines rows from two tables where the ON condition matches, such as an enrollment's course_id and a course's id.
notes: JOIN and INNER JOIN mean the same thing.
AS e and AS c are table aliases. They let you write e.grade instead of enrollments.grade.
An inner join drops rows with no match: Zoe has no enrollments, so only Diego appears in the last result.
pitfall: When both tables have a column with the same name, you must say which one. SELECT id FROM students JOIN courses ON ... gives Parse error: ambiguous column name: id.
